essay:
Michael Hurley died on April 1, 2025, in Astoria, Oregon, at 83 — quietly, on his own terms. The obituaries all reached for the same word: 'godfather.' Godfather of freak folk, godfather of outsider Americana. He recorded his first album in 1964 for Folkways on the same reel-to-reel machine that had captured Lead Belly's final sessions.

He was never part of the Village folk-revival scene of Dylan and Ochs, even though he was right there in New York at the same moment — instead he drifted toward the Holy Modal Rounders' lane of gleeful, ramshackle weirdness, wrote a werewolf into a country waltz, and kept making records — something like 30 of them — until the year he died.

This playlist traces Hurley's actual family tree: the Holy Modal Rounders (the band he orbited without officially joining), the 1976 'Have Moicy!' supergroup, and the two-generations-deep chain of disciples who kept his songs alive — Cat Power, Yo La Tengo, Vetiver, and Will Oldham, who has been explicit about the connection. An Americana UK writer pointed out that Hurley's 1971 'Light Green Fellow' — skeletal fiddle, lonesome guitar, a menacing/tender ambiguous narrator — 'prefigured Will Oldham's Palace Brothers by a couple of decades.' You can hear it.
